claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: 1. The database preflight probe now replaces every driver message with one fixed sentence, and the operator has no way to read the real reason. In `src/sqllens/preflight.py` the SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL arms all render the detail as `f"{type(exc).__name__}: connection failed; check connection settings."`, and the only two places that print a `PreflightError` (`src/sqllens/cli.py`, in `serve` and in `validate`) print the message alone and never the chained `__cause__`. A wrong password, an unreachable host, a missing database and an unreadable SQLite file therefore all look identical to the person running the command. The SQLite arm is the weakest case for the trade, because a `sqlite3.Error` message describes a local file the operator configured themselves and cannot carry a remote credential. (raised by 2/5 agents)
